title: ACEIT brings the paper-roster case to council
summary: Anoka County Election Integrity Team (ACEIT) educates Oak Grove officials on why paper check-in rosters are lawful, auditable, and under local control—and how electronic poll pads change the information picture on Election Day.
detail: Refine exact workshop date when Jan 2024 materials are available. ACEIT later published a statutes video arguing the county misread poll-pad law.

title: Oak Grove votes for paper
summary: City Council passes a 4–0 resolution to switch back to paper poll books. Other Anoka cities, including Ramsey, move in the same direction.
detail: Sample cancel-e-poll-pad resolutions are published for towns and cities on projectminnesota.com/local.

title: County letter threatens felonies for paper
summary: Anoka County Elections sends a multi-page unsigned letter warning precinct head judges that using paper poll pads could mean felony exposure. Later process questions about authorship and signing are labeled as questions, not conclusions.
detail: Host or link the letter only after Erik clears the PDF for public use.

title: Courts asked to clarify municipal choice
summary: Upper Midwest Law Center petition to the Minnesota Supreme Court (A26-0910) seeks clarity that municipalities may choose paper or electronic rosters. Educational focus: what statutes say versus what staff asserted.
detail: Add docket and filing links when Erik confirms which materials may be linked or hosted.

title: Act while paper remains a local option
summary: Compare the 2023 electronic-tabulator lock-in pattern: once statutes harden a practice, local choice shrinks. Councils and citizens who want auditable paper check-in should move while statutes still leave room—and ask auditors for the data that is public. Clearer published data is common ground.
detail: Next local steps: sample resolutions, attending council, and public-record how-tos (phase v2).
